OP:+.Definition: The addition operator {c:code-ex}+{/c} adds two numeric values together or concatenates two string values.

OP:-.Definition: The subtraction operator {c:code-ex}-{/c} subtracts the right-hand value from the left-hand value.

OP:+:UnaryPlus.Definition: The unary plus operator {c:code-ex}+{/c} returns its operand's value unchanged.

OP:-:UnaryMinus.Definition: The unary minus operator {c:code-ex}-{/c} computes the numeric negation of its operand.

OP:*:Multiplication.Definition: The multiplication operator {c:code-ex}*{/c} multiplies two numeric values.

OP:*:Dereference.Definition: The dereference operator {c:code-ex}*{/c} accesses the value stored at the memory address contained in a pointer.

OP:/.Definition: The division operator {c:code-ex}/{/c} divides the left-hand value by the right-hand value.

OP:%.Definition: The modulus operator {c:code-ex}%{/c} returns the remainder after dividing the left-hand value by the right-hand value.

OP:++.Definition: The increment operator {c:code-ex}++{/c} increases a numeric value by one.

OP:--.Definition: The decrement operator {c:code-ex}--{/c} decreases a numeric value by one.

OP:=.Definition: The assignment operator {c:code-ex}={/c} assigns the right-hand value to the left-hand target.

OP:+=.Definition: The addition assignment operator {c:code-ex}+={/c} adds the right-hand value to the target and stores the result back in the target.

OP:-=.Definition: The subtraction assignment operator {c:code-ex}-={/c} subtracts the right-hand value from the target and stores the result back in the target.

OP:*=.Definition: The multiplication assignment operator {c:code-ex}*={/c} multiplies the target by the right-hand value and stores the result back in the target.

OP:/=.Definition: The division assignment operator {c:code-ex}/={/c} divides the target by the right-hand value and stores the result back in the target.

OP:%=.Definition: The modulus assignment operator {c:code-ex}%={/c} divides the target by the right-hand value and stores the remainder back in the target.

OP:&=.Definition: The bitwise AND assignment operator {c:code-ex}&={/c} applies a bitwise AND and stores the result back in the target.

OP:|=.Definition: The bitwise OR assignment operator {c:code-ex}|={/c} applies a bitwise OR and stores the result back in the target.

OP:^=.Definition: The bitwise XOR assignment operator {c:code-ex}^={/c} applies a bitwise exclusive OR and stores the result back in the target.

OP:<<=.Definition: The left shift assignment operator {c:code-ex}<<={/c} shifts the target's bits to the left and stores the result back in the target.

OP:>>=.Definition: The right shift assignment operator {c:code-ex}>>={/c} shifts the target's bits to the right and stores the result back in the target.

OP:>>>=.Definition: The unsigned right shift assignment operator {c:code-ex}>>>={/c} shifts the target's bits to the right without preserving the sign bit and stores the result back in the target.

OP:&:BitwiseAnd.Definition: The bitwise AND operator {c:code-ex}&{/c} compares the bits of two values and produces a 1 in each position where both bits are 1.

OP:&:AddressOf.Definition: The address-of operator {c:code-ex}&{/c} obtains the memory address of a variable and produces a pointer to it.

OP:|.Definition: The bitwise OR operator {c:code-ex}|{/c} compares the bits of two values and produces a 1 in each position where either bit is 1.

OP:^:BitwiseXor.Definition: The bitwise XOR operator {c:code-ex}^{/c} compares the bits of two values and produces a 1 in each position where the bits differ.

OP:^:Index.Definition: The index-from-end operator {c:code-ex}^{/c} specifies a position counted from the end of a sequence, where {c:code-ex}^1{/c} refers to the last element.

OP:~.Definition: The bitwise complement operator {c:code-ex}~{/c} flips all the bits of a value. Zeros become ones and ones become zeros.

OP:<<.Definition: The left shift operator {c:code-ex}<<{/c} moves the bits of a value to the left by the specified number of positions.

OP:>>.Definition: The right shift operator {c:code-ex}>>{/c} moves the bits of a value to the right by the specified number of positions, preserving the sign bit.

OP:>>>.Definition: The unsigned right shift operator {c:code-ex}>>>{/c} moves the bits of a value to the right by the specified number of positions without preserving the sign bit.

OP:!:NullForgiving.Definition: The null-forgiving operator {c:code-ex}!{/c} suppresses nullability warnings, asserting to the compiler that this value is not null.

OP:!:LogicalNot.Definition: The logical NOT operator {c:code-ex}!{/c} reverses a boolean value. {c:bold}true{/c} becomes {c:bold}false{/c}, and {c:bold}false{/c} becomes {c:bold}true{/c}.

OP:&&.Definition: The conditional-logical AND operator {c:code-ex}&&{/c} returns {c:bold}true{/c} only if both conditions are true. It stops evaluating as soon as one condition is false.

OP:||.Definition: The conditional-logical OR operator {c:code-ex}||{/c} returns {c:bold}true{/c} if at least one condition is true. It stops evaluating as soon as a true condition is found.

OP:<.Definition: The less-than operator {c:code-ex}<{/c} checks whether the left-hand value is smaller than the right-hand value.

OP:>.Definition: The greater-than operator {c:code-ex}>{/c} checks whether the left-hand value is larger than the right-hand value.

OP:<=.Definition: The less-than-or-equal operator {c:code-ex}<={/c} checks whether the left-hand value is smaller than or equal to the right-hand value.

OP:>=.Definition: The greater-than-or-equal operator {c:code-ex}>={/c} checks whether the left-hand value is larger than or equal to the right-hand value.

OP:==.Definition: The equality operator {c:code-ex}=={/c} checks whether two values are equal.

OP:!=.Definition: The inequality operator {c:code-ex}!={/c} checks whether two values are not equal.

OP:..:Range.Definition: The range operator {c:code-ex}..{/c} creates a range from a start index (inclusive) to an end index (exclusive). Either endpoint can be omitted to indicate the start or end of the sequence.

OP:..:Slice.Definition: The slice operator {c:code-ex}..{/c} matches or captures zero or more elements at this position in a list pattern.

OP:=>:Lambda.Definition: The lambda operator {c:code-ex}=>{/c} separates the parameter list of a lambda expression from its body.

OP:..Definition: The member access operator {c:code-ex}.{/c} navigates to a member of the preceding type or instance, such as a property, method, or field.

OP:?..Definition: The null-conditional operator {c:code-ex}?.{/c} accesses the specified member only when the preceding value is not {c:color-blue keyword}null{/c}, returning {c:color-blue keyword}null{/c} otherwise.

OP:::.Definition: The namespace alias operator {c:code-ex}::{/c} accesses a type or namespace within an aliased namespace. The left-hand side must be a namespace alias, an extern alias, or the {c:color-blue keyword}global{/c} keyword.

OP:??.Definition: The null-coalescing operator {c:code-ex}??{/c} returns the left-hand value if it is not {c:color-blue keyword}null{/c}, otherwise returns the right-hand value.

OP:??=.Definition: The null-coalescing assignment operator {c:code-ex}??={/c} assigns the right-hand value to the target only if the target is currently {c:color-blue keyword}null{/c}.

OP:->.Definition: The pointer member access operator {c:code-ex}->{/c} accesses a member of the struct that a pointer points to.

OP:c?t:f.Definition: The conditional (ternary) operator {c:code-ex}c ? t : f{/c} evaluates a boolean condition and returns one of two values — the first if the condition is {c:bold}true{/c}, the second if it is {c:bold}false{/c}.
